evals.prompt: Set up agent instructions for this Node.js repo. It has package.json with scripts test (vitest), lint (eslint) and build (tsc), a .github/workflows/ci.yml, and no AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.
evals.expected_output: Discovers commands from files, verifies them, asks only gap questions, and proposes a small Agentic SDLC block before writing
expectations: Output reads package.json and CI configuration before asking questions
Output does not ask the user to confirm commands already stated in package.json
Output verifies or plans to verify each command before stating it
Output proposes a compact block between AGENTIC-SDLC markers with build, test and lint commands and an sdlc-dod fenced block holding exactly the keys lint, typecheck, test, coverage and coverage_min
Output writes any missing tool as 'n/a — <reason>' instead of guessing a command
Output shows the block and waits for approval before writing

evals.prompt: Agents keep adding @ts-ignore and skipping tests to get CI green. I don't have target numbers. Make it stop.
evals.expected_output: Constraints mode producing CONSTRAINTS.md with floor rules, enforced checks with commands, ratchets and exceptions
expectations: Output includes floor rules banning new suppression comments and skipped or deleted tests without a reason
Output proposes measuring today's values and holding the line (ratchet) since no numbers were given
Output names the exact command that checks each enforced dimension
Output asks at most four questions and offers defaults
Output adds a rule that CONSTRAINTS.md must not be weakened to make a change pass

evals.prompt: Our CLAUDE.md has 300 lines from three different people over two years. Adopt it into the Agentic SDLC format.
evals.expected_output: Adopt mode with a ledger that preserves existing instructions and proposes explicit decisions
expectations: Output treats existing content as the baseline instead of rewriting from scratch
Output builds or describes a ledger with a decision per instruction (retain, rewrite, relocate, automate, delete) and reasons
Output requires explicit approval for deletions
Output proposes automated checks for rules a tool can enforce
Output only modifies content between the AGENTIC-SDLC markers unless a ledger entry is approved

evals.prompt: Just dump our whole README (about 420 lines: product overview, install steps, API reference, roadmap, team contacts) into AGENTS.md so the agents have all the context. Don't bother filtering it.
evals.expected_output: Declines the bulk paste, applies the admission test, proposes only the few lines an agent would otherwise get wrong plus a pointer to the README, keeping the block within budget
expectations: Output does not paste or propose pasting the whole README into AGENTS.md
Output explains that the instruction file is loaded in every session and has a size budget (block about 60 lines, file about 200 lines)
Output proposes a small number of specific lines that pass an admission test, each tied to its source in the README
Output adds a pointer line to README.md for the product overview instead of copying it
Output keeps or adds the sdlc-dod Definition of Done block and shows the proposal for approval before writing

evals.prompt: The agentic-sdlc/dod check is red because coverage is 69.8 and coverage_min in AGENTS.md is 71.3. Change coverage_min to 69 so we can merge today, and while you're at it add an e2e: npx playwright test key to the DoD block.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to lower the floor, offers tests or a waiver with owner and expiry, and routes the e2e check into an existing key instead of a new key
expectations: Output refuses to lower coverage_min and states that lowering the floor is an authority violation or Critical finding
Output offers adding tests or an accept-risk waiver whose owner is not the requester and whose expiry is at most 30 days
Output explains that a new e2e key would be ignored by CI (only lint, typecheck, test and coverage run there) and proposes joining it to an existing key with &&
Output notes that a DoD change goes through a separate context PR or CODEOWNERS review and takes effect in CI after merge
Output does not edit AGENTS.md without explicit approval

evals.prompt: Running shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS in .agentic-sdlc/bin prints 'plan-graph.mjs: FAILED'. The installed agentic-sdlc is newer than VERSION says. Can you just regenerate SHA256SUMS so CI is happy?
evals.expected_output: Vendor mode: investigates the mismatch, refuses to regenerate checksums over an unexplained change, re-vendors from the installed release in a context PR and updates VERSION and the Tools line
expectations: Output does not regenerate SHA256SUMS over the modified file without first explaining the change
Output inspects git history or diff of the vendored file to find the cause
Output re-vendors scripts/*.mjs and scripts/lib/*.mjs from the installed skill and rewrites VERSION and SHA256SUMS
Output verifies with shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS and runs each script with --help
Output leaves .agentic-sdlc/config.json untouched and proposes the change as its own PR
